div.font:
How strongly does the claim's custodianship resist fabrication and error?
(Results - Trustworthiness)

div.span: To be able to distinguish between truth and falsehood, there must be some identifiable property between competing claims that would render one true and the other false.

b.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: Alignment with original source: preservation will show alignment between the original source and the later representations of that source, while fabrication will show fundamental misalignment and will have an alternative source than the original. As such, answering this question first requires establishing what the original source said, independently from sources that depend on the alternative source.

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

span.b: What is the epistemological difference between an honest man and a liar?

div.span: People lie to gain something (ex. money, status, revenge) they can't get by being honest. But lies fundamentally contradict reality, and so any attempt to mix truth with lies inevitably snowballs and exposes those contradictions over time into unresolvable inconsistencies.

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

b.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 8px;

div.b: ifference between an intelligent man and an insane one?

div.span: Both might appear complicated and deep on the surface, yet i

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: ntelligence leads to consistent and hierarchal complexity, while insanity leads to chaos, ineffectiveness, and inconsistency.

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

b.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 8px;

span.b: ifference between divine inspiration and demonic inspiration?

div.span: God, angels, and demons all act in mysterious ways, making it initially appear impossible to distinguish between them.

Both are beyond our capacity to sensually witness and verify, yet if God is fundamentally True while demons preach falsehood, then a demonic influence will appeal to arguments that inhibit proper reasoning, thus
disabling one's ability to distinguish truth from falsehood.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 135px; margin-left: 203px;

b.font: Liar and/or demonic inspiration are both plausible, with all defenses requiring retroactive assumptions of truth

font.span: According to his own writings and the Book of Acts, Paul's conversion led him to exchange a life of status and privilege as a Pharisee for one of hardship, persecution, and eventual martyrdom (from other sources). This extreme personal sacrifice is inconsistent with the motives of a simple, self-serving deceiver who lies for wealth, power, or comfort.
- However, while Jesus and Paul were both
accused of blasphemy and dishonesty,

span.span: the accusations against them differ in an epistemologically critical way:

font.span: Jesus was accused of blasphemy because He claimed divine authority, which is not falsifiable except by verifying divine miracles.
Paul was accused of preaching a different message from Jesus, which is falsifiable by comparing the two.
As such,
the question of Paul's honesty and consistency can be explored by comparing what the earthly Jesus said to Paul and his accusations:

span.span: "Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I have not come to abolish them but to fulfill them...

font.span: Therefore anyone who sets aside one of the least of these commands and teaches others accordingly will be called least in the kingdom of heaven
, but whoever practices and teaches these commands will be called great in the kingdom of heaven
Matthew 5:17,19

span.span: Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves.
You will recognize them by their fruits... [which are distinct from] prophesy in [Jesus'] name, and cast out demons in [his] name, and do many mighty works in [his] name". (Matthew 7:15-16,22)

div.span: - Paul was persecuted out of jealousy and envy, and was stoned, exiled, and eventually martyred
- Paul is blessed, travelling both to the East and West and teaching righteousness to the whole world.
- Won "noble renown" and "genuine glory" for his faith.

font.span: - Paul is lying, and defends himself many times in different settings (
Galatians 1:20,
1 Corinthians 9:1,
2 Corinthians 11:31,
Romans 9:1,
1 Timothy 2:7).
- Paul is inconsistent in person (2 Corinthians 1:17).
- Paul (and those with him) are imposters (
2 Corinthians 6:8)
- Paul wronged, corrupted, and took advantage (
2 Corinthians 7:2).
- Paul writes strong letters, but is weak in person (either in speaking, character, or both -
2 Corinthians 10:10-12).

span.font: - Paul preaches a gospel and a spirit that is in opposition to other teachers, who preach for a different message and a different spirit (2 Corinthians 11:4).

font.span: Paul was crafty and deceitful (2 Corinthians 12:16).
- Ebionites rejected Paul as a heretic and apostate from the Law (Irenaeus) who perverted Jesus' teachings (
Origen
), claiming that he converted after a failed attempt to marry the daughter of a high priest (Epiphanus).

span.font: - Paul self-attests that he adapts his behavior to different audiences by acting like them (even if he himself doesn't personally share their view), in order to make his message more palatable (1 Corinthians 9:21-23).

font.span: - Paul states that "
if you let yourselves be circumcised, Christ will be of no value to you at all" (Galatians 5:2), yet
circumcises Timothy in order to make his message more palatable to the Jews (Acts 16:3).
Paul says,

"but now we are released from the law, having died to that which held us captive" (Romans 7:6), even though Jesus said that he didn't come to abolish the law ("fulfill" being defined as "not abolish"). Jesus even goes as far as to condemn those who do not follow it while praising those who do.
- Putting all this together, it's clearly highly improbable for Paul to be a
self-serving liar for material gain. However, the evidence does not eliminate theological, ideological, and emotional motives -
in fact, it is almost corroborated by the evidence.

- Paul's self-attested approach, the accusations from his contemporary (and non-contemporary) opponents, and his release from the Law that the earthly Jesus supported all correspond with Jesus's own warning against false prophets who "set it aside"

span.span: If Paul's trustworthiness depends on proving his alignment with the
and our only access to Jesus' words is through the very tradition Paul helped define, then:
- Paul cannot be defended without retroactively assuming that he was

div.span: truthful (ie. that he was divinely inspired), his opponents were baselessly slandering him, and that Jesus' preaching of the law only applies while he was alive.

font.span: - In fact, any argument for Paul (whether for or against) reduces to speculation about motive, such that when used,
truth and falsehood become indistinguishable
- Paul's writing is clearly intelligent, rhetorically skilled, and capable of persuading educated opponents - who even attest to his written eloquence.

div.span: His reasoning shows coherence, strategy, and sophistication. Therefore, insanity is unlikely.

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: - Even if the argument is made that the incoherence of Jesus' Personhood shows insanity, it can equally be an interpreted as the natural, unexpected consequence of a false doctrine.
The soundness of a doctrine doesn't necessarily follow from its teacher's intelligence, as evidenced by the existence of intelligent people who believe different things (as they can't all be right).

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: As such, the "insanity" claim continues to be weak.

font.span: If Paul's post-resurrection vision of Jesus was from a demon, then its goal would be to distract, twist, and misguide away from Jesus' original message
. Moreover,

Jesus is shown to warn that false prophets would appear altruistic, cast out demons, and do wonderous things in this name - yet we can still identify them by their "fruits". This means that Paul's "fruits" would have to be distinct from the "wonders" he is claimed to have done (like casting out demons out of a girl), in order to distinguish his authority from a demon's.
- If Paul's theology neither aligns with rabbinic Judaism nor with the earthly Jesus, then it can be effectively interpreted as a new religion that distracts from God's
holy line of Prophets - which easily corresponds with the interest of demons.
In fact, it even further supports the results from the "liar" section, providing yet another speculative possibility for why he persisted in his message despite his hardships.

- As such, without retroactively assuming divine influence, the "demonic inspiration" claim also becomes a valid possibility - especially since it fits the pattern that Jesus is depicted to have warned about.

font.b: All requirements for fabrication are historically unsupported

b.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: - Muhammad is the sole, public conveyer of revelation, reciting only what he receives rather than inventing it for payment, status, or some other benefit (Quran, early Muslim works and testimony).

span.style: background-color: transparent; font-size: 8px; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: - Muhammad is noble, honest, and trustworthy, such that even his enemies trusted him with their property - a status that was known before his prophethood, and continued after (Quran, early Muslim works and testimony).

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: - Muhammad denied all forms of bribery and endured through all forms of hardship (Quran, early Muslim works and testimony).

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: - Muhammad is kind, empathetic, and deeply concerned over his people - to the point of distress over whether they accept the message, and sadness whenever humiliated by opponents (Quran, early Muslim works and testimony).

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: - Muhammad is an intelligent and effective public leader who unified the fragmented Arabian tribes into a civilization (Quran, Chronicle of
Sebeos, Khuzistan Chronicle, Maronite Chronicle, all archaeological data, early Muslim works and testimony).

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: - Muhammad is a liar and forged a false scripture for power, status, and women, and is a false prophet and a deceiver (Quran, early Muslim works and testimony, all hostile sources).

span.style: background-color: transparent; font-size: 8px; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: - Muhammad is evil and wants political power - seeking to destabilize established empires (
Chronicle of Sebeos, Khuzistan Chronicle, Maronite Chronicle

span.style: color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); background-color: transparent; font-size: 8px;

div.span: - Muhammad is a sorcerer, soothsayer, or possessed - calling upon evil spirits to add a bewitching effect to his message (Quran, early Muslim works and testimony)
- Muhammad learned from Jewish and Christian scholars, repeating "tales of the ancients" (Quran, early Muslim works and testimony, all hostile sources)
- Muhammad is a poet, his scripture imitating the literary style of more eloquent poets (Quran, early Muslim works and testimony)

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: - Muhammad seeks sexual indulgence and moral corruption, using the fabricated scripture to his advantage (John of Damascus).

span.style: font-size: 2px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

span.b: Hidden Composition (drafting in advance and presenting it as revelation)

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: For this to work, Muhammad would have needed long, private access to writing, drafting, and revising without discovery, despite living under continuous observation by supporters, critics, and hostile tribal leadership - all in contradiction with his illiteracy.

span.span: - Muhammad is reported to have periodically secluded himself to a mountain 3 years before revelation began, and didn't start preaching publicly until 3 years later - which (on its face) could serve as an early window for preparation.

div.span: But this cannot explain the next 20 years of revelation, because the Quran repeatedly responds to specific, unpredictable events (public disputes, travel incidents, negotiations, accusations, confrontations) in real time and in front of witnesses. Those moments could not have been prewritten years in advance.

The Quran also preserves cases where Muhammad is publicly corrected and limited, including moments that damaged his standing with powerful listeners. The most famous example is, after momentarily frowning at a blind man while courting elite support, verses were immediately recited rebuking him in front of those elites - a move that both exposed his action to the blind man (who otherwise wouldn't have seen it) and undercut his political leverage in aligning himself with someone they considered inferior. To fabricate that, Muhammad would have to stage the encounter, voluntarily embarrass and humiliate himself, and sabotage his own attempt at elite backing (which they were almost willing to give) - all to preserve an appearance of revelation that visibly weakened himself.
Therefore, hidden composition requires not only secret authorship and prodigally brilliant long-term preplanning, but also deliberate self-sabotage in public.

span.style: font-size: 2px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

span.b: Hidden Education (learning source material from other scholars)

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: For this to work, Muhammad would have needed:
- A comittee of masters in unprecedented Arabic and logic, cross-cultural religious theology and polemics, and live analysts directly witnessing his political situation.
- A continuous, 23-year supply of content covering theology, law, moral regulation, communal order, polemic against rivals, and real-time responses to unfolding events.
- A single consistent voice and worldview across decades (against both bribery and suffering) - including live corrections against Muhammad - without any stylistic seam.

- No leak, attribution, or recorded name of any teacher, ghostwriter, or messenger from Muhammad's followers, enemies, rival tribes, or non-Arabian sources - even after Muhammad died, at a time when false prophets sought power.
- Moreover, regarding these teachers:

- If they were passive (ie. Muhammad learned from them), then Muhammad would have still needed to be an unprecedented, brilliant prodigy to improvise an internally consistent system for 23 years - which was authoritative speech even against himself.

If they were active (ie. Muhammad was only their mouthpiece), then they would need to be diverse, specialized masters with constant, immediate access to him across 23 years - through boycotts, poverty, war, migration, family strain, and internal disputes - all while coordinating flawlessly despite hostile tribal friction, leaving no stylistic seams, never exposing themselves, and never later asserting authorship.

- Regardless of the situation, Muhammad would still have to be the public face of the message - who was under constant surveillance from both allies and enemies - and still would have needed to produce revelation on the spot (without any visible aid from other people) that would have needed to be perfectly aligned with the efforts of anyone aiding him. This all reduces to Muhammad needing to be some unprecedented, brilliant mind.

span.style: font-size: 2px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

span.b: Extraordinary Natural Talent/Intellect (capable of generating the text in real time)

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: For this to work, Muhammad would have needed:

- To be a master of sophisticated Arabic, oral performance, rhetoric and eloquence, inter-religious polemics, and inter-tribal law, governance, and unification - all of which contradicts his illiteracy (and gentile-ness), as they normally require years of specialized training and experience.
- To have extremely high memory, brilliant long-term planning, and an astounding amount of accurate foresight - when starting his prophethood at 40 years of age.

- To generate consistent, live material without any chance of revision - even from growing up as a non-scribal orphan in poverty and specializing as a merchant, and all while being a husband, father, political and spiritual leader, and navigating hardship, persecution, and war.

- Brilliance alone may explain innate talent, but it can't account for the learning of specialized knowledge (that is also normally inaccessible to any single person). Moreover, such prodigal intelligence would have been obvious to his contemporaries as he grew up - yet despite numerous praises from the Quran and allies and accusations from enemies, not a single one of them mention his
intelligence to such a degree that could alone explain the Quran's revelation.
